meta.channelLabel: CHILI LAB Japan / Headphones, Down Low
meta.conceptLabel: EP013 골목 산책 — 오래된 동네를 걸으며 어린 시절 이야기를 나눔
meta.setIdentity: CHILI LAB episode 013: one old-neighborhood walk told through low rap or sing-rap verses, short melodic hooks, close mature vocals and recurring street details. The music stays recognizably Chill Rap / Urban Soul before any genre variation is considered.
meta.crossSetDifferentiation: EP011 established shared music taste; EP012 changed the temperature through late replies. EP013 moves that new closeness offline into an old neighborhood walk and childhood stories. No confession, relationship label, hand-holding milestone, missed-last-bus overnight scene or first portrait event is allowed here; EP014 remains reserved for the first time they photograph each other.
meta.genrePolicy: Seven coherent families: chill rap/jazz-hop, neo-soul/lo-fi soul, alt-R&B/tape-soul, garage/microhouse/dub, acoustic soul-hop/bossa-jazz, jazz-soul duet, broken-beat/dream-soul. At least ten tracks retain clear CHILI LAB rap, sing-rap or spoken-sung DNA.
meta.instrumentPolicy: Reuse a restrained common city palette while rotating one foreground color: baritone guitar, Wurlitzer, nylon guitar, upright piano, Hammond, vibraphone, marimba, muted trumpet, mellow flute, cello pizzicato, tape piano, upright or fretless bass, dub guitar delay.
meta.rhythmPolicy: Low-to-mid energy only. Rotate broken trip-hop, soft 2-step, bossa-jazzhop, loose jazz-hop, neo-soul rim pocket, acoustic soul-hop, microhouse, brushes, broken beat, mellow boom-bap, lo-fi soul, dub and downtempo pulse without three consecutive identical kick/snare grammars.
meta.vocalPolicy: Close mature vocals with varied resonance and articulation. Rap tracks stay behind the beat and narrative; mixed tracks use sing-rap verses plus short melodic hooks; three song-centered tracks provide contrast without turning the set into R&B ballads.
meta.lyricPolicy: Scene first, emotion second. Every song belongs to the same neighborhood walk and reveals one childhood detail through a physical place or object. The emotional movement is curiosity to trust, not romance escalation. Avoid repeating hand, shoulder, eyes or smile as default devices. Final track lightly seeds EP014 by mentioning a camera only as a next-time possibility, without taking a picture in EP013.
meta.rapRatioPolicy: 5 rap-centered, 7 mixed, 3 song-centered; no three consecutive tracks share the same ratio.
meta.killingPointPolicy: Every track has one 8-15 second Signature Moment. Most use executable lyric variation, vocal handoff or a 2-4 note instrument answer. Unreliable micro-events such as one-beat silence or bass removal are kept only inside killingPointDesign and are not treated as guaranteed Suno behavior.
meta.energyArc: 1-4 enter the old neighborhood and establish place; 5-9 turn childhood details playful and vivid; 10-14 become more personal without romantic escalation; 15 returns to the station and opens the door to EP014.

songs.lyrics:
[Intro - 4 bars instrumental]
[Verse 1 - 16 bars, low rap]
Same station name, different ticket gate,
you say the old exit moved two doors east.
A florist took the place of the newspaper stand,
the clock above the stairs is five minutes slow.
Yesterday we talked until the screen went dim,
today the air feels easier than the messages did.
You point past the taxis toward a narrow lane,
and say the real neighborhood starts that way.

[Pre-Hook - 4 bars]
No map, no plan, no reason to hurry,
you know every turn before it arrives.

[Hook - 8 bars, melodic]
This Way First,
show me where the small streets start.
This Way First,
let the main road disappear behind us.

[Verse 2 - 16 bars, low rap]
Corner pharmacy changed its sign twice,
the noodle shop still keeps chairs outside.
You tell me which crossing felt enormous at nine,
which alley looked longer walking home alone.
I listen more than I answer this time,
because every block has a story before I got here.

[Instrumental Break - 8 bars]
[Final Hook - 8 bars]
This Way First,
now the title sounds less like directions.
This Way First,
the old street opens one turn at a time.

songs.lyrics:
[Intro - 8 bars instrumental]
[Verse 1 - 16 bars, rap]
Clinic sign changed, shortcut didn't,
space between two buildings still too narrow for cars.
You say you were told never to take it after dark,
which of course meant everyone took it after dark.
Drain cover, back door, old air-conditioner,
three landmarks for a fifteen-second rebellion.
At eleven it felt dangerous,
now it barely fits two adults side by side.

[Hook - 12 bars]
Take the Shortcut,
small fear, short road, long memory.
Take the Shortcut,
we know where it comes out now.

[Instrumental Chorus - 16 bars]
[Verse 2 - 16 bars, rap]
I tell you the alley I wasn't supposed to use,
and how every town apparently invents the same warning.
You say rules get smaller when retold,
I say maybe streets do too.

[Break - 16 bars instrumental]
[Final Hook - 16 bars]
Take the Shortcut,
shortcut gets one delayed guitar answer.
No fear left to prove tonight,
Take the Shortcut.

[Intro - 4 bars instrumental]
[Verse 1 - 16 bars, sing-rap]
Streetlight clicks on before the sky is finished,
you check the time and say six-twenty, almost exact.
That used to be the signal nobody admitted following,
one more round, one more throw, then home.
Somebody's window would open on the third floor,
a voice would carry farther than phones ever did.
You say the light made the whole block feel borrowed,
like night belonged to older people first.

[Hook - 8 bars]
When the Light Came On,
the street changed rules without a sign.
When the Light Came On,
every game had one more minute.

[Verse 2 - 16 bars, sing-rap]
I tell you my clock was a shop shutter,
metal noise rolling down at nearly seven.
Different signal, same negotiation,
childhood measured by what happened outside.

[Instrumental Break - 8 bars]
[Final Hook - 8 bars]
When the Light Came On,
[Female low harmony: came on]
now we keep walking after it wakes.

[Intro - 4 bars instrumental]
[Verse 1 - 16 bars, Female sung]
There, below the newer paint line,
a short scratch beside a faded date.
You say someone measured you against this wall,
then argued the mark was one finger too low.
You were angry for a week about one centimeter,
which is the kind of fact no photograph would explain.

[Verse 2 - 16 bars, Male sung]
I tell you mine was pencil on a kitchen frame,
a different town, a different wall.
Every year someone wrote the date too lightly,
and every year I stood too straight on purpose.
I have not thought about that in years,
until your small scratch gives it back.

[Hook - 8 bars, split duet]
[Female] Still
[Male] There
[Both] a mark too small to carry all that time.

[Instrumental Break - 12 bars]
[Final Hook - 16 bars, reversed duet]
[Male] Still
[Female] There
[Both] two different walls, the same ridiculous need to be taller.

[Intro - 4 bars instrumental]
[Verse 1 - 16 bars, Male spoken-sung]
Station sign comes back between the buildings,

You name five things that disappeared,
then six that somehow refused to change.
I know the blue gate, the four-ten clock,
the cracked fourth step, the light at six-twenty.
A few hours ago they were only your details,
now I can place them in the right order.

[Hook - 8 bars, Male melodic]
Same Street, New Story,
old corners, different company.
Same Street, New Story,
we leave the rest where it belongs.

You say I talk more on streets I already know,

No need to name what changed since last night,
we already spent a whole neighborhood proving it did.

[Male] Same Street
[Female] New Story
[Both] next time we can start somewhere neither of us knows.
